gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many minutes a 16-inch MacBook Pro needs to reach 50% at the watts each charger's laptop port keeps once a second device is plugged in: Apple's 99.6 Wh battery and '50% in around 30 minutes' work out to about 100 W average into the battery, so a port held at 100 W has no margin and a port held at 65-70 W needs at least 43-46 minutes.
standout_why: Compared against thegadgetmasters.com (cited; says multi-port chargers 'redistribute' but gives no split numbers), Macworld (cited; prints per-port watts and some splits, no battery Wh, no minutes), thisusb.com (prints Anker's 100 W + 40 W split and says the Mac port 'drops to 100W or less', but no time cost), specsource.org (prints W per 100 g on total watts, no splits), thunderboltlaptop.com (no splits) and Apple's support page (the 30-minute claim only). Rivals hold the inputs; none converts kept watts into minutes against the 99.6 Wh battery. It stops short of 3 because I could not open a maker table or named test giving the two-device split for the UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W 5-port or the Anker Prime 160W.
decides: It confirms that every row should be ranked on 140 W from one port used alone, and it puts a cost on sharing. A 140 W-total charger (Anker A2697, AOHi The Youth, Baseus PicoGo 140W) drops the Mac to 100 W or 65-70 W with a second device, which is at or below what Apple's 30-minute claim requires. A 160 W-total charger (UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W, Anker Prime 160W) has 20 W of arithmetic headroom above 140 W, but that only decides the pick if a maker table shows the 140 W + 20 W split, which I did not source. Notebookcheck's 56-58 W reading with all five ports busy shows the UGREEN does not hold 140 W when full.

findings.label: Average watts into the battery that Apple's claim implies (derived)
findings.note: 0.5 × 99.6 Wh ÷ 0.5 h = 99.6 W. Inputs: Apple's 99.6 Wh and Apple's 'around 30 minutes' (support.apple.com/en-us/102378). Battery-side average; the adapter must supply more to cover conversion loss and the running laptop.

findings.value: at least 21 minutes; Apple states around 30

findings.note: 49.8 Wh ÷ 140 W × 60 = 21.3 min. Floor only: assumes every watt at the port reaches the battery and the laptop draws nothing.
